paraphrase: Earth, sprouts and similar effects have a maker, because they are effects, like a pot; the maker of the world must know its material causes and the merit and demerit of selves — an omniscient Lord.
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: Section-level summary from memory; not checked against a local text.

paraphrase: Subjecthood (pakṣatā) is the absence of certainty (of the probandum in the subject) unaccompanied by a desire to infer; hence one can infer even what is known if one wishes to, and cannot infer what is certain if one does not.
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: Section-level summary from memory; not checked against a local text.

paraphrase: Inferential cognition is produced by 'consideration' (parāmarśa) — the cognition of the probans as pervaded by the probandum and present in the subject — not by the bare memory of pervasion.
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: Section-level summary from memory; not checked against a local text.

paraphrase: Gaṅgeśa's own definition: pervasion is the co-location of the probans with a probandum that is not delimited by the delimitor of the counterpositiveness of any absolute absence which resides in the locus of the probans and is not co-located with its own counterpositive.
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: Paraphrase of a highly technical definition from memory; to be checked word by word.

paraphrase: Five provisional definitions of pervasion are examined — e.g. 'not occurring in what possesses the absence of the probandum', 'not occurring in what possesses the absence of the probandum and differs from what possesses the probandum', 'not co-located with a mutual absence whose counterpositive is what possesses the probandum', 'being the counterpositive of an absence located in all that possesses the absence of the probandum', 'not occurring in what is other than what possesses the probandum' — and rejected, chiefly because they fail where the probandum is present everywhere (kevalānvayin).
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: The first four definitions are confirmed in the local Vyāptipañcaka commentary e-text; the fifth is from memory.

paraphrase: An erroneous cognition is the apprehension of a thing as having a property it lacks (e.g. mother-of-pearl as 'this is silver') — misplaced apprehension — not a mere failure to grasp the difference between two cognitions.
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: Section-level summary from memory; not checked against a local text.

paraphrase: Validity is not grasped by the cognition that apprehends a cognition (otherwise doubt about validity could not arise); it is known extrinsically, by inference — e.g. from the success of the activity it prompts — and it is produced by an excellence in the causes of the cognition.
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: Section-level summary from memory; not checked against a local text.

paraphrase: Verbal cognition arises from words when there is expectancy, compatibility and proximity among them and the speaker's intention is known.
speaker: Gaṅgeśa
notes: The Yogyatāvāda and Tātparyavāda section headings are confirmed in the local e-text; the summary is general.

paraphrase: Now verbal testimony is examined: a word (statement) produced by true knowledge of the meaning that is the cause of its utterance is a means of knowledge.

paraphrase: Therefore the validity of the Veda, ascertained from its acceptance by the great, rests solely on its being rooted in the perception of Īśvara, which is the ground of trust and depends on nothing else.
